question: In a climate that is not changing, what is the chance that year 100 of a record sets a new high, in percent?
move: In a steady world records grow rarer, so a cluster of them is a signal.
ask: When records keep piling up in my life, have I asked what has changed underneath?
trap: Assuming new records stay as common as in the first few years.
hint: Ask how many years could equally be the warmest so far.
steps: With no trend, each of the 100 years is equally likely to be the warmest
So year 100 has a 1 in 100 chance
reference: Benestad, How often can we expect a record event?, Climate Research, 2003
